title: Rav Huna bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s student, as in Kiddushin 70a, where Rav Yehudah said to Rav Nachman: “Does the Master not hold what Rav Huna bar Idi said that Shmuel said?” etc. In Midrash Tehillim 22:28 is his precious homily on the verse David said, “Save me from the lion’s mouth; from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me” (Psalms 22:22): when David was tending the sheep he found a wild ox sleeping in the wilderness and thought it was a mountain, and climbed on it. When the wild ox woke and stood up, it lifted him to the heavens, and David vowed that if the Lord saved him he would build a Temple a hundred cubits high, like the horns of the wild ox. The Holy One, blessed be He, summoned a lion; when the wild ox saw the lion, it crouched before it; when David saw the lion he was afraid of it. The Holy One, blessed be He, summoned a deer; the lion leapt after it, and then David came down from the wild ox’s horns and went his way. This is what David said: “Save me from the lion’s mouth, just as You answered me from the horns of the wild ox.” But Yalkut, Tehillim, remez 688, reads Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi.

notes.text: במרבר is read as במדבר. The wild-ox narrative remains an attributed homily, with the alternative Yalkut Yaakov bar Idi name retained rather than silently harmonized with Huna.

The consulted Midrash Tehillim passage is numbered 22:22, while Hyman supplies 22:28. It names Huna bar Idi and the wild ox, but has the ox kneel and David descend before his fear of the lion, without a deer in that passage. Hyman’s deer-and-lion sequence remains his account. The exact supplied subsection and Yalkut 688 witness were not independently verified; the reported Yaakov bar Idi variant therefore remains Hyman’s account.
